newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Expelled African National Congress (ANC) KwaZulu Natal MP Sifiso Nkabinde held two public meetings on Tuesday to mobilise support against the ANC, and warned the party that it would trigger a new "war" if it "interfered" with his support base in the volatile province.

- Zaire's warrring parties reached agreement in Pretoria late Tuesday on five key points aimed at finding a peaceful solution to the country's crisis while the rebels, led by Laurent Kabila, continued to move in on the southern city of Lubumbashi.

- About 4.4 billion rand is set to flow into the money market in the next three months in the form of Telkom's share of its privatisation proceeds - creating a monetary policy challenge for the Reserve Bank.
- The rand has remained remarkably firm in the face of a rampant dollar, causing some economists to ask whether it might not be in danger of getting too strong.
- British transnational chemical company Thor Holdings on Tuesday made a nine million rand settlement in a UK civil court case brought by 20 South African workers.

- Fears of an ecological disaster grew on Tuesday, with Western Cape authorities starting a crackdown on people who illegally removed crayfish which "walked out" of the sea at Elands Bay on the west coast.
- The curator of the CAF Pension Fund, Tony Mostert, said on Tuesday that he had applied successfully for the provisional liquidation of Corporate Acceptances Finance.
- Engen, the listed oil company, has been left with a tiny stake in Mossgass, the state owned oil-from-gas producer, after it settled a legal wrangle with the Central Energy Fund.
- Amalgamated Appliances (Amap), a small appliance manufacturer and importer that was unbundled from Malbak, would list on the JSE early next month, the company said on Tuesday.
- The government should adopt "a pragmatic rather than an ideological approach" to the privatisation of South African Airways, Mac Maharaj, the transport minister, said on Tuesday.

- Nissho Iwai, the Japanese trading conglomerate, which is South Africa's second-largest Japanese trading partner, is planning a big investment in a non-ferrous metal refinery in South Africa, the company said on Tuesday.

- Minutes of a State Security Council (SSC) meeting that have been handed to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission point to the direct involvement of top National Party leaders - including former president F W de Klerk - in the formation of a "counter-revolutionary" third force.

- Sharply conflicting visions of how to beat back the crime wave lay behind the clash between police commissioner George Fivaz and Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi, sources said on Tuesday night.
